summary: Backend-only testing of EtherLens AI v2 features. Added /app/backend/tests/test_v2_features.py (11 tests) covering /api/flows, /api/flow/stream (TCP reassembly), /api/pcap/export (round-trip parsed back with scapy), /api/pcap/export 404 when empty, /api/geo/{ip} (private + public), /api/topology?enrich=true, /api/settings/webhooks GET/POST persistence, /api/settings/webhooks/test with bad URL and empty URL. All 11 tests passed (100%). Previous iteration_1 v1 tests (15) remain intact.

minor.issue: Rebuilds packets from stored hex via Ether(raw); packets whose hex failed to re-parse are silently dropped. Not a bug but worth noting.
ip-api.com is HTTP (non-HTTPS) and rate-limited to 45 req/min. Behavior is correct (graceful 'note' fallback) but external dependency is a soft failure point.
_load_settings() is only awaited on FastAPI startup; if Mongo is unreachable it silently uses in-memory defaults. OK for scaffold.
Enrichment is awaited inline inside the request handler; a slow ip-api.com response blocks the whole topology endpoint for up to ~4.5s per batch.

action_items: Optional: cap geo-enrichment total wait time (currently timeout per 90-ip batch=4.5s) and run it as a background task so /api/topology?enrich=true never blocks UI.
Optional: skip rebuilding failed hex packets explicitly in /api/pcap/export and surface a count in the response (how many packets were exported vs stored).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:28-30 — uses os.environ['MONGO_URL'] and os.environ['DB_NAME'] (KeyError if missing). Fine but no defaults, which is the required pattern.

analysis.py:_assemble sorts chunks by seq but de-dup is by exact seq match only — overlapping/retransmitted TCP segments with different seqs but overlapping byte ranges are NOT merged. For noisy simulated traffic this is acceptable; for real captures it will produce slightly inflated/duplicated payloads.
analysis.py:reassemble_stream filters only TCP-family protocols. UDP/HTTP3 flows (and any flow stored as 'UDP') are silently empty on /api/flow/stream — matches /api/flows filter so consistent.
webhooks.py uses blocking `requests.post` in asyncio.to_thread — OK, but no retry/backoff. If Slack/Discord 429s a burst of threats, they are dropped silently (fan_out swallows exceptions).
geo.py uses a module-level asyncio.Lock plus module-level _cache. In uvicorn --workers > 1 this cache would not be shared; for current single-worker setup it is fine.
server.py:ws_endpoint — stats_task is now initialized to None before try (iteration_1 recommendation already applied).
server.py: no explicit auth on /api/settings/webhooks — any client can read/overwrite webhook URLs. Add a shared secret / IP allowlist before shipping.
test_credentials: N/A — no auth in this backend.
context_for_next_testing_agent: V1 regression suite is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (15 tests). V2 feature suite is at /app/backend/tests/test_v2_features.py (11 tests). Both run under /app/backend/pytest.ini with -n 2 --dist loadscope. New endpoints: /api/flows, /api/flow/stream, /api/pcap/export, /api/geo/{ip}, /api/topology?enrich=true, /api/settings/webhooks (GET/POST), /api/settings/webhooks/test. The public preview URL returned 502 for ~2 minutes during a hot-reload reloader restart on first attempt; `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` recovered it. If re-testing and seeing 502s, wait or restart backend before failing.
rca of the issue: Initial run failed with ReadTimeout because file edits triggered a uvicorn --reload restart, and the reloader worker had not come back up (ingress returned 502 for ~60s). After `supervisorctl restart backend` and an 8s wait, all 11 tests passed in 9s.
